classification.difficultyReason: Choose the positions of one flag colour; the other colour fills the remaining positions, matching the taught example.

content.prompt: How many ways can 3 identical red flags and 3 identical purple flags be arranged in a row?

spec.sourceRegion: Question 12, six-flag row beneath the stem
spec.description: Six rectangular flags in a horizontal row, three red then three purple, with white regions above and below each central coloured band.
spec.mathematics: Two classes of identical objects, with three objects in each class.
spec.answerVisibility: Supplied illustration only; no arrangement count is shown.

answer.short:
$20$ arrangements.

Choose the three red-flag positions from six; the purple flags fill the remaining positions.
answer.worked:
Choose 3 of the 6 positions for the red flags. The remaining positions are filled by the purple flags.
$$\begin{align*}\binom{6}{3}&=\frac{6!}{3!3!}\\\binom{6}{3}&=\frac{6\times5\times4}{3\times2\times1}\\\binom{6}{3}&=20.\end{align*}$$
There are 20 arrangements.
